P1.evidence: Pre-call information existed and was used, but inaccurately. The rep twice cited Trevor's DMs — 'I also heard from Trevor, you want to lose some body fat' and 'I understood from Trevor that you mentioned something about... maybe you didn't see the progression that you wanted to see in your workout so far' — and the second was wrong, drawing a correction: 'No, I'm actually pretty happy with the progression I made.' He also had the prospect's weight from the application ('at the moment you're 84 kilos, right?'). The frame carried two parts of four — 'dive into what you're currently doing, see where you want to go, see if we can help you bridge that gap' — with no what's-in-the-way or what-you-need, and no agreement was sought. The open question was never asked; Brent simply started talking after the frame.

P2.evidence: The training-and-food half was run well and the person half was skipped entirely. Injuries were the standout: asked directly ('do you have any injuries, things that we should know about? Because I know football can sometimes bring those things'), then qualified for chronicity ('Is it like a nagging pain, or is it something that just comes up here and there?'), which is what surfaced the meniscus tear and the physiotherapist. Training week, results and nutrition were all properly covered, including a genuinely good probe on drinking frequency that moved a vague 'I let it hang a little bit' to 'probably eight out of ten' weekends. Against that: age was asked at 00:08:34 almost as an afterthought, weight was read off the application rather than asked, height never came up, occupation was never asked despite 'I have a busy job' being volunteered and being the ICP-deciding fact, health conditions were never asked, and sleep and energy were never asked at all.

P3.evidence: The surface layer was handled cleanly — the 1-to-10 mobility scale, the specific fat location, stamina, the functional-versus-strength distinction. The bridge ran with a comparison frame: 'a lot of people in Netherlands that are just okay with it... So I am curious, why do you think it's important for you to still go to that next level?' That produced the best material in the call: training discipline spilling into work performance. But the depth question hit a wall the rep did not try to get past — 'it's not that deep that I don't feel good at the moment... It doesn't impact my life negatively' — and he accepted it. Who-else-does-this-impact was never asked despite a live-in partner, and nothing was driven toward relationship, identity or longevity. The recap was a factual goal list, not a reframe. Partly a genuine constraint: this prospect has no pain to excavate, which is itself the finding.

P4.evidence: The phase's premise does not hold here and that has to be scored honestly. Brent has trained consistently for three years, tracks his lifts and is satisfied with his progress — there is no failed attempt to root-cause, so why-it-didn't-stick and the information-isn't-the-problem line drop out as not applicable. The training history was gathered but as background rather than as diagnosis. What the rep did do well was ask the prospect to define the requirement himself — 'like just lay it out to me. Like what are the main things that you feel like that is what I would need?' — which produced an unusually precise answer: 'someone to review my current training and say, okay, I would maybe change this, this, and this. And on day A, you can do kettlebell training... But yeah, still with my current gym schedule mixed into it.' That is the gap named in the prospect's own words, which is what P4e asks for.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form. No two-year question, no settle question, no why-not, no line in the sand. Unlike the other calls in this batch, the omission is at least coherent: the prospect had explicitly said his current state does not hurt him ('It doesn't impact my life negatively at the moment'), so there is no cost of inaction to make real, and the rep had already decided to route him to a lower tier. Scored a miss rather than not applicable because the phase was reachable and simply not attempted — but the coaching note is that the script has no version of Phase 5 for a prospect with no pain, and that is a script problem, not a rep problem.

P6.evidence: The belief question was asked only about the lower tier and only in a truncated leading form — 'when it comes to that, do you feel like, yeah. Yeah. That is something I see myself doing' — with the rep supplying the answer himself before the prospect spoke. P6b never ran. P6c failed visibly and is the clearest coachable moment in the call: on the strength of 'Sounds interesting', the rep said 'Perfect. Let's get you started with that', and the prospect immediately came back with 'Yeah. What do you mean with getting started?' That is the script's own warning playing out — moving forward without a clear yes — and it cost the close on a $200/month product.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted on the lower tier, so the phase applies, but payment was never asked for once — the rep went from 'Let's get you started' straight to sending a link when the prospect asked for more information. Steps 2 and 3 are not applicable because the onboarding call with Trevor and the coaching agreement belong to the one-to-one product, which was not sold. Step 4 has a partial analogue that the rep did run: he told the prospect to check the link, to post his introduction in the community, said 'let me know when you've joined', and set a check-in one to two months out.

objection_plays.detail: A third script gap, alongside the two already logged in playbook.json. The prospect is not resisting price, timing, a spouse or fear — he is a satisfied, consistent trainee who wants to bolt kettlebells onto a programme he likes and does not want a transformation. 'It's not that I want to quit regular gymming for 100%' and 'I think my question is just a bit different maybe than what you're offering.' None of OA to OE apply. The rep handled it credibly by surfacing the mismatch himself before presenting price — 'is it that you're really looking for full guidance, or are you maybe looking for just something to try out first?' — and then routing to the lower tier. But there is no scripted path, no defined lower-tier pitch, and the improvisation lost the sale on the tier he did present.

Second gap: the prospect asked for something the product does not do — a review of his existing gym split with kettlebell days blended into it, plus nutrition tips. The rep's own words disqualified the offer from serving it: 'he isn't like an expert in the gym, like he's not a personal trainer or anything.' There is no scripted move for a hybrid-programming request, and no asset to hand a prospect who wants adjunct programming rather than a replacement.

'Maybe if you can just send me what it actually all means, then I could just have a look at it' is a soft think-about-it, on a $200/month decision, from a prospect who had just said price does not shock him. No move ran. The rep sent the link, confirmed the phone number and closed the call. Even a single 'do you feel this can get you what you're after?' would have been in bounds.

notes: Score this one on judgement rather than on phase coverage: the rep spotted a scope mismatch early, refused to force a $6,000 transformation onto an adjunct buyer, and pre-framed price honestly at 'at least four figures' rather than anchoring. That is the right call and the debrief with his setter the same day shows he knew why. What he then did badly was sell the alternative — no commitment check, no ask for payment, and a link sent in place of a close on a product the prospect had already said he liked the sound of. Two systemic items to escalate rather than coach: there is no scripted lower-tier pitch, and the injury screening was good enough to surface an unhealed meniscus tear but stopped short of asking whether the physiotherapist had cleared the specific programme being sold.
